saw_lines: Parents rarely join a kids sports program on impulse. They compare the sport, the age group and the schedule first.
So the sale is won in the ad’s first line, where a parent decides whether the sport fits their child.
Your 30 live ads carry no proof number, so collect one real figure like families enrolled and lead three new ads with it.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 27 Oct 2026
points: None of your 30 live ads shows a number that shows buyers can trust you, so parents have no reason to believe the claim. Collect one real figure, like families enrolled, and lead three new ads with it on the creative.

4 of your 16 copy ads open on the same “it’s simple” invite line, so one opener competes with itself for the same parents. Test two new angles against it, the season price and the first practice, and keep the stronger one.

None of your 16 copy ads mention an offer, so a parent has no reason to sign up today. Put a first enrollment offer or sibling bundle in line one of three new ads, and test it against your price angle.

15 of your ads have run 60+ days, so they already work, but a single creative leaves nothing to rotate in when it tires. Build three more variations of the oldest winner, changing only the photo and first line.

ads_1: Proof-led family creative with a first enrollment offer, tested against the invite hook
soc_1: Brand social strategy across Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, X and YouTube
